lessons.title: Leading and Following
lessons.summary: One person decides, the other surrenders. Light dominance and submission, with clear agreements.
lessons.content:
In games of leading and following, one person takes over the decisions for an agreed time: where, how, how fast, when. The other hands over control. That can be very liberating, for both sides. The foundation is trust, and trust needs agreements.

Before the game
Clarify three things:
What is explicitly wanted?
What is possible, but only after asking?
What is off limits, no discussion?
Agree on the duration, for example half an hour, and on your stop word. With the stop word the game ends immediately, and nobody is offended.

Ideas to start with
Whoever leads gives clear instructions: “Lie down.” “Don't move.” “Look at me.”
Whoever follows may only touch or come with permission.
Whoever leads sets the pace, holds back, rewards.
A firm grip on the wrists, a slap on the bottom, if that was wanted beforehand.

Whoever leads carries responsibility
Leading doesn't mean being reckless. Whoever leads keeps watching: breath, face, body tension. When in doubt, ask briefly: “Colour?” Green, yellow or red.

After the game
After intense games, care is important, often called aftercare: holding, covering up, water, kind words. Some feel vulnerable or wired afterwards, even hours later. Talk about it again the next day.

The task
Each of you writes your three lists, wanted, maybe, off limits, and compare them. Then play for half an hour with one person leading. Next time you swap.
lessons.reflection_question: Which role felt surprisingly good to you, and what did you learn about yourself?
